segmentName: Transformer Radiators (cooling equipment for power/distribution transformers)

market.worldSizeUSD_B_range: Estimates diverge notably: $1.85B (2024) to $3.65B by 2033 (8.9%/yr) per one source; $2.8B (2025) to $4.7B by 2034 (5.9%/yr) per another. This is a genuinely niche sub-component category with poor data-source consistency — the broader transformer cooling device market (radiators, fans, oil pumps, heat exchangers) is estimated at 5-7%/yr (2026-2035) globally.
exportGeographies: Gulf/Middle East (per Tarang Engineering's own footprint)
globalCompetitors: Wilson Transformer Company — note these are primarily transformer OEMs, not radiator-specialist peers
market.domesticSlice: Asia-Pacific drives >50% of absolute value increase in the broader transformer cooling device market; Africa/Middle East shows the highest percentage growth (8-10%/yr) as utility infrastructure expands

structureFacts: Demand is structurally tied to the broader power-transformer/grid-expansion market (rural electrification, renewable grid integration, substation capacity additions), since radiators are an accessory/cooling component to transformer production, not a standalone demand driver
Rising electricity demand from data centers, EV charging networks, and urbanization is cited as an emerging driver of cooling-equipment demand generally

adoptionStructure.note: Back-to-back/ancillary supply contracts driven by transformer OEMs' own order books — not an independent repurchase-rate category

drivers: utility/PSU vendor approvals (PGCIL, RDSO, state electricity boards)
on-time delivery tied to transformer production schedules
customerValue.strongestPredictor: utility/PSU vendor-approval status, especially for high-voltage-class (e.g. 765kV) transformer programs

steps: offer pressed-steel, hot-dip galvanized, stainless-steel, gooseneck/flanged/offset radiators
maintain multi-plant footprint near transformer-manufacturing clusters
hold utility/PSU vendor approvals (PGCIL, RDSO, state electricity boards)
deliver on-time tied to transformer production schedules
receive back-to-back/ancillary supply contracts driven by transformer OEMs' own order books
fulfil against utility tenders/EPC project schedules
